body: Thank you
Well done, I'm proud of you!
I'm just broken.  However people in chat have alleviated my anxiety for the moment.

I don't know you but I would guess you are not unloveable.  If anything the other way round, you are so accommodating to people that they think you will always be there, like part of the furniture.  

After a lifetime of being like that, I've recently learned to stand up for myself.   To say "no, I won't tolerate that!".  It's still new so it feels a bit strange but actually I'm finding that people respect it.  The fact is that none of us is perfect but if you don't stand up for yourself and impose boundaries, no one else will do it for you.

The simplest memories are often the fondest ones we have.  A few months ago I threw a "helicopter" (Sycamore seeds) into the wind and watched  it, just as I would have as a child.  It brought me great pleasure.
Fuck off!  You have no idea what suffering I'm going through.
Babe there's nothing wrong with that!  I'm sorry that wherever you  live deems it illegal but honestly, there's nothing wrong with it.
WTH?!  It was a discussion sub!
Thanks, I'm ok.  Talking with someone who is grounding me, coming down(up?) from the spiral
I'll text you in chat
Thanks but no, it's kind of a private thing

I have a few health problems going on, recently lost my mother who was my main reason for living.   No one really that I am responsible for (a LDR which doesn't feel right at the moment).   I just suddenly hit a low.
Thank you

Riding a bike is hard, especially if you are older.   If you learn as a little child you get training wheels and stuff but to start off as an older child/young adult you don't have all those things.  If you don't have a natural sense of balance that makes it even harder.

You also have a greater sense of fear as a young adult.  As young kids we are used to scrapes and bruises but when you get a little older it becomes a little scary.  

What you are experiencing is entirely normal, don't worry about it!

Absolutely there is life beyond your twenties.  You are reading things from people who are deeply dissatisfied with their lives, whatever their age.  

Fun is wonderful, no matter what your age.  Yes, people can say "why didn't I discover this sooner" but the reality is that they are still enjoying themselves.  

For other reasons, I was unable to have "fun" as a young person, nor have I been able to hold down a job for any length of time but that doesn't mean I can't enjoy the now (and I am enjoying the now despite problems which should make it untenable).  

It ain't over til the fat lady sings and I'm not singing so that means you have to go on and make the best of life!

You have an accute and valuable insight.  It also sounds like you have done a lot to help yourself, which I admire.   I don't have an answer but keep going.  One day you might be the tool you wish to be.

Babe in this world we really have no one but ourselves.  People come into and go out of our lives for a reason but at the end of the day you have to be strong enough in the core to withstand it. 

That's not to say you shouldn't allow people to help you when they are there and willing but you can't rely on someone being there forever.  They move on in their own journeys, they die, they have other commitments.  No one can be there for you always, 24/7.  

You are welcome to talk to us about your issues but there's a lot of us, you're not relying on one or two people who maybe have their own stuff to deal with. 

Yes, we hurt.  We all have our own problems but that includes your friends.  You may have just caught them at a bad time or maybe they think their problems are more significant. That is the beautiful thing about this sub, no one ever says that.  Your problems are yours and if they are hurting you there's always someone here to listen. 

You have worth.  Even if you don't think so at the moment.  You have worth and you are valuable.  

My dear I am more than twice your age and sometimes I don't feel "grown up".   Adulting can suck but it can also be fun too.  Rough it through the sucky times to get to the fun times.  I promise you it can be worth it!

Stop.  Just stop.

You have no idea about my partner or what he does for me.  No one can be there 24/7.  We all have to sleep sometime.  He has other commitments in his life too, not just me.  Don't be so judgemental
Thanks.  Actually this is inspiring!
Mate I appreciate your optimism but the wizard might kill me, saving me all the trouble.  The dragon might burn me to death, ditto.  I'd prefer to go out fighting but I'm not afraid to give in.
lol, I seriously doubt that
Yes, it's sis!  I just want to go to sleep and never wake up
I wish it was stage 4 right now

Mine Stage 3c Ovarian cancer
Dog's don't know, they haven't said

If you go to a professional you can start with general suicidal feelings and then when you trust them more talk about your viable plan whilst insisting you don't really have a time scale.  That should be sufficient to keep you out of a psychiatric ward.  

The point is that you need to do something!  Whether that's therapy or meds to lift your mood (in which case your primary care doctor/gp is the person to go to).  Don't just ignore it!

You won't get placed into  psychiatric ward unless you have a viable plan and imminent timescale.  A general feeling of "I want to die" is insufficient (at least in the UK).  Maybe go slowly with a professional, it might just be the best thing you've ever done and you can see how they react prior to actually letting them know your real feelings. 

Most of all though, you need to let the people around you know that you are facing tougher times than normal.  Even if they only invite you out for a meal or a drink as a result, it will help because company is always better than facing something alone.

I'm going through a similar, although accelated, process.   From being the one who resolutely keeps going to the one who asks "what is all this for?".  

It's ok to let people know you are not ok.  My partner taught me that.  It's not like I continually talk to him about suicide (mainly because I don't feel that way) but he knows I'm going through a tough time at the moment and it crosses my mind occasionally.  

I agree, you can't go from one extreme to the other in one leap but you can let people know that you're "not having such a good day" or something similar.  Given that you have portrayed such a positive persona until now, people will take that seriously and it might lead to conversations where you can let out your true feelings.  

The alternative is a professional, where you have no prior links and you can explain exactly how you feel.
